claim_scope: source and failure-causality research before implementation; no controller state, panel identity, waveform, temperature, production, residue-free or visual claim
WHY_WORSE: The rejected added-first candidate produced two electrophoretic activations for every changed logical frame and hard-reset before both passes; the captured partial run reached 94 activations before the owner stopped it.

The owner observed more residue. Repeated activations and interrupted controller state are plausible contributors, but the exact physical cause is not proven without controller-state and panel-bound waveform evidence.
CUTOFF_CAUSE: Pass 1 deliberately excluded every mixed-transition byte. Any new leading-edge pixel sharing a byte with an old pixel being removed could not appear in the first visible state.

The first activation was therefore intentionally incomplete; pass 2 later restored the missing current-frame content in the previous-black bounding box. This topology explains the owner-observed disappearing/eaten segment that then returned.
PROVEN: COMP-REQ-255 is a permanent physical NO_GO: other residue increased and the original disappearing/eaten movement segment remained.

SSD1681 Rev0.13 command 0x2D returns eleven Display Option bytes; response bytes 2 through 6 correspond to register 0x37 bytes B through F, response byte 6 bit 6 is the Mode2 RAM Ping-Pong selection, and bytes 7 through 10 are waveform version.
SSD1681 Rev0.13 command 0x2F exposes Chip ID in bits 1:0; the diagnostic contract additionally requires busy bit 2 to be zero.
The Good Display exact marketed T03 public sample uses SSD1681 at 200x200 and contains no 0x2D read or 0x37 write in its normal/fast/partial path.
The supplied one-second EPAPER.c is immutable input and its SHA256 remains 7EE1F8D5184B7883D1CADF745B724A6C12915E74F82641E4CB31764B07CD9896.
INFERENCE: A stable read of Mode2 RAM Ping-Pong may explain whether controller-internal RAM selection matters to future one-activation experiments, but it does not itself prove the physical panel uses a residue-controlled partial waveform.
The prior two-pass reset/activation topology plausibly worsened accumulated residue; that causal contribution is an inference rather than a controller-internal measurement.
UNKNOWN: Whether the current physical 0154BN-D67-D2 FPC is manufacturer-bound to the exact marketed GDEY0154D67-T03 public sample.
Whether Mode2 RAM Ping-Pong is enabled in this controller OTP/display-option state before the read.
The panel-bound partial waveform, its temperature rules and any complete CWF1 classification.
Which physical old/new waveform state, if any, the controller associates with RAM command 0x24 versus 0x26 for this panel and mode.
A RAM X/Y window limits controller RAM addresses written; neither the datasheet nor current evidence proves that the electrophoretic physical scan is limited to that rectangle.
Public black/white RAM mappings do not authorize treating 0x26 as an arbitrary old-frame plane. No such assumption is allowed in this Goal.
